Method of Attack: Phishing campaigns delivering remote access tools (RAT) to steal corporate data
Use of fake subscription emails impersonating brands (Zoho, MasterClass, Duolingo) to lure victims
Sending scam emails from Gmail accounts with fake invoices attached
Social engineering via phone calls to instruct victims to install remote access tools
Installation of multiple RATs for redundancy and persistence
Use of commercially available remote desktop solutions (Atera, AnyDesk, Synchro, Splashtop)
Manual installation of reconnaissance and data exfiltration tools (SoftPerfect Network Scanner, SharpShares, Rclone)
Impacted Systems: Corporate systems accessed via remote access tools
Attack Vector: Phishing emails with fake subscription renewal notices and attachments
Indicators of Compromise: Nearly 90 domain names used for phishing and data exfiltration, including domains resembling Zoho, MasterClass, and Duolingo
Emails sent from Gmail accounts impersonating legitimate brands
Use of RAT tools: Atera, AnyDesk, Synchro, Splashtop
Use of network reconnaissance and data exfiltration tools: SoftPerfect Network Scanner, SharpShares, Rclone
